extracted.intended_audience: IP office staff, policymakers, researchers, and analysts using WIPO patent/trademark statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and definitions for how WIPO compiles and reports patent and trademark statistical metrics (e.g., application/grant counts, class counts, origin vs office data, procedural timings). Useful for analysing and comparing office-level IP statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application class count (trademarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: A trademark application may refer to different classes of goods or services. Many offices use the Nice Classification, an international classification of goods and services for registering trademarks and service marks. Applications received at these offices are classified in one or more of the 45 Nice classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains single-class vs multi-class filing (some offices allow single-class only; others permit multi-class). To improve international comparisons of numbers of applications received, compare class counts across offices. Class counts are used to make trademark registration activity internationally comparable and have been used since 2004 (first year with complete class count data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent application class count
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed at some regional IP offices are equivalent to multiple applications in countries that are members of the organizations establishing those offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: for the EUIPO each application is multiplied by the corresponding number of EU member states (in 2019 multiplier = 28). An application filed with the EUIPO by a non-EU applicant is counted as 28 applications abroad; an application filed by an EU resident is counted as 1 resident application and 27 applications abroad. The same multiplier is applied to classes specified in the applications. The equivalent application class count concept is used for reporting data by origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resident vs non-resident (office data vs origin data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark applications received by offices from resident and non-resident applicants are referred to as office data, whereas applications filed by applicants at a national/regional office (resident applications) or at foreign offices (applications abroad) are referred to as origin data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use origin-based statistics (residence of applicant) to complement office-based data. Resident filing shares and non-resident shares vary substantially by office; e.g., in 2019 residents accounted for 84.3% of global filing activity. When analysing cross-country activity note whether the statistic is by office (where filed) or by origin (where applicant resides).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and interpretation of the Nice Classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Many offices use the Nice Classification (45 classes) to classify goods and services in trademark applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because some offices restrict filings to single class while others allow multiple classes, comparing raw application counts can be misleading — use class counts for better comparability. See www.wipo.int/classifications/nice for the classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent applications/grants by origin may be incomplete
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Equivalent applications by origin data are incomplete because some offices do not report by origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnote caution: when using equivalent-by-origin figures, be aware of missing origin reporting from some offices which can make origin-based aggregates incomplete or biased.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offices acting as receiving or national offices for PCT
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes on receiving-office roles: (c) The International Bureau acts as the receiving office for PCT applications. (d) The African Intellectual Property Organization (OAPI) acts as the receiving office for PCT applications. (e) The Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property (IFPI) acts as the receiving office for PCT applications. (f) The African Regional Intellectual Property Organization (ARIPO) acts as the receiving office for PCT applications. (g) The African Intellectual Property Organization (OAPI) acts as the national office for patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These procedural roles affect how applications are counted by office and by origin; be careful when attributing PCT filings to national offices versus regional/International Bureau receipts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of missing/NA values in tables
rubrics_metrics.description: ".. indicates not available. n.a. indicates not applicable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When parsing tables, treat '..' as data not available and 'n.a.' as not applicable. Several offices/rows may show '..' or 'n.a.' which affects totals and completeness of series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural data fields: total applications processed; granted; rejected; withdrawn/abandoned
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural table columns include: Total applications processed; Granted; Rejected; Withdrawn or abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the primary counts used to summarise office activity. Note that procedural differences across offices (see rejection recording) affect comparability of these columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences in 'rejection' and 'abandonment' recording across offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Every effort has been made to compile procedural data based on common definitions and concepts, but procedural differences make it extremely difficult to fully harmonize such data. For instance, “rejection” is not recorded as a final decision in Canada. Applicants are informed of the action that they must take or questions that they must answer in order for their application to be considered, and if an applicant cannot provide the required information, they are regarded as having abandoned the application. A similar situation exists in Australia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing 'rejected' vs 'withdrawn/abandoned' across jurisdictions, adjust for local recording practices (some offices treat what others call 'rejection' as 'abandonment').

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of examiners (FTE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of examiners is reported as FTE (full time equivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTE standardises staffing counts; note the appended note: 'FTE is full time equivalent.' Use FTE when comparing office examiner capacity rather than headcount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-to-action metrics: First office action and Final office decision (months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables report 'First office action (months)' and 'Final office decision (months)' as measures of pendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are median/average (as reported) months to first action and to final decision. Because procedural practices differ across offices, these timings should be interpreted with caution when making cross-office comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant/Equivalent-grants caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Equivalent grants by origin data are incomplete, because some offices do not report by origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar to equivalent application caveat — origin-based grant counts may be incomplete. Use with caution when attributing grants to applicant origins.
